$EDSA

I gave this to you a month ago at $1.20. 💰

In just about a month, this is now up 680%. 💸

Check screenshots below to see the guidance I provided for this trade every step of the way to make sure that your trade is MAXIMISED to the fullest potential. 

You don't see me talk about this as often today after the initial move is done because I am always focused on finding new actionable setups for all of you here.

But it doesn't mean I'm not riding shares! 

My philosophy for trading small caps is simple;

> Find a good actionable position, take entries.

> Trim profits on the way up and raise your stops accordingly.

> Most importantly, if trend does not break down, if our position isn't threatened, I'll ride it out as high as I can get.

The thing about small caps is that they are very good at making multi-bagger moves if trend holds. Think $AXTI and $IREN when they were both in the $1.00 area price point.

Those two companies may not necessarily be small caps but the concept stays the same on the initial stages of the trade until fundamentals and thematic changes takes over the rally. 

Most people ask for targets but the truth is none of us can really know where a stock will go even on the next minute.

Let the stock market do the work in pushing the price up. All you need to do is to manage your risk.

If trend holds, hold rest for more.

If trend fails, cut remaining position to maintain a green trade. 

Keeping things simple goes a long way. Don't over-complicate things when they don't need to be.

MARITIME ENCOUNTER | BRP Miguel Malvar (FFG6) was conducting a sovereignty patrol within the Philippines’ EEZ near Sabina Shoal when a PLA-Navy vessel (bow no. 622) directed its fire control radar toward the ship on March 07, 2026.

The Philippine Navy immediately issued a radio challenge in accordance with standard procedures, prompting the vessel to stow its radar and de-escalate.

The incident underscores the importance of restraint and adherence to international law. The Philippine Navy remains committed to lawful patrols, the protection of sovereign rights, and the peaceful, rules-based resolution of disputes in the West Philippine Sea.

BURNING UP, FIRE ☀️

The sun aligned perfectly in front of the Oblation statue at the University of the Philippines Diliman on March 19, 2026 at little past 6 PM, just a day before the March equinox.

The March equinox signals the start of spring in the northern hemisphere and autumn in the southern hemisphere. During this time, the sun sits directly above the equator, bringing nearly equal hours of day and night worldwide, according to PAGASA.

PHOTOS COURTESY: Ronin Bautista via DZUP

I am Alexandr Wang. I became a billionaire at 25. The youngest self-made billionaire in the world.

My company is Scale AI. We are valued at $14 billion. Our clients include OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft, Google, and the United States Department of Defense.

We sell data. Specifically, we sell labeled data. The labeled data is what makes AI work. Without it, a language model is a very expensive random number generator. Every image a self-driving car recognizes. Every sentence ChatGPT understands. Every piece of content Instagram removes. Someone labeled that. A human. In a loop.

My company does not label the data. My company operates a platform called Remotasks. Remotasks hires the humans.

The humans are in Kenya. The Philippines. India. Venezuela.

They are college-educated. Many have degrees in mathematics, engineering, computer science. They cannot find work in their own economies. Youth unemployment in Kenya is 67%.

They are not employees. They are taskers. Independent contractors. No health insurance. No severance. No union. Contracts measured in days. Some weekly. Some monthly. None permanent.

They are paid $1.50 to $2 per hour.

I need to be precise about that number. OpenAI agreed to pay my subcontractor, SAMA, $12.50 per hour per worker. SAMA paid the workers $2. The difference is operational overhead. That is what we call it.

A data labeler in Nairobi earns $2 per hour to teach ChatGPT how to think. ChatGPT earns OpenAI $2 billion per month.

The labeler does not know they work for me. A 2023 investigation found that workers on Remotasks did not know Remotasks was a subsidiary of Scale AI. My company's name does not appear on their platform. Their platform's name does not appear on my website. This was not an accident.

The work is not just tedious. Some of it is horrific.

Content moderators review murders, beheadings, child abuse, sexual assault, bestiality. Eight hours a day. A survey of 76 workers in Kenya, Colombia, and Ghana documented 60 independent incidents of psychological harm. Anxiety. Depression. PTSD. Panic attacks. Substance dependence. One worker read 700 sexually explicit and violent texts per day. He lost his family.

They are bound by NDAs. They cannot speak about what they see.

In March 2024, I shut down Remotasks operations in Kenya. The workers received an email hours before the shutdown. The email said, effectively, "fare thee well." Thousands of young people who depended on the platform for their livelihood were left with nothing.

A Kenyan civil rights activist called it "modern-day slavery." That was on 60 Minutes. CBS. Prime time.

I did not respond.

The workers formed a union. The African Content Moderators Union. They lobbied for better conditions.

My clients moved the work away from unionized workers. The outsourcing companies then fired the unionized workers to win the contracts back.

The union was effective for approximately four months.

In Kenya, a court ruled that Meta could be sued for its role in this system. Meta argued that Kenyan courts had no jurisdiction over an American company. They lost. They appealed. They lost again. 140 workers were diagnosed with severe PTSD.

I am 25 years old. I am worth $2 billion. I was on the cover of Forbes.

The people who built my fortune cannot afford therapy for the trauma they sustained building it. They earn $16 per day. Therapy in Nairobi costs $50 per session.

The AI industry is projected to be worth $1.3 trillion by the end of the decade.

The data labeling market that underpins it will reach $13.7 billion by 2030.

The workers who do the labeling wrote an open letter to the President of the United States. They called their conditions "modern-day slavery." The letter was published on foxglove. It received press coverage for one news cycle.

Then the cycle moved on.

I sell the thing that makes AI intelligent. The thing is human judgment, purchased at $2 per hour, from people who are not allowed to tell you what they saw.
